name: SLC5A3
summary: SLC5A3, foal immunodeficiency syndrome (FIS) - a fatal recessive disorder of the immune system and blood, found in the Fell Pony and the Dales Pony. A single change in the gene (c.1337G>T, p.P446L) alters a transporter of myo-inositol; how that causes the disease is not understood. An affected foal looks normal at birth and dies within about three months. A carrier is healthy. A 2011 screen found 38 percent of Fell Ponies and 18 percent of Dales Ponies to be carriers.

phenotypes.name: Wild type
phenotypes.description: Two working copies. Nothing is wrong and nothing is passed on.

phenotypes.name: SLC5A3 carrier
phenotypes.description: One copy of fis. The horse is completely normal and there is no way to see it - but half its foals inherit the copy, and two carriers bred together are the only way foal immunodeficiency syndrome appears.

phenotypes.name: Foal immunodeficiency syndrome
phenotypes.description: No working B cells and a failing marrow. The foal looks normal at birth and within weeks develops severe, worsening anaemia and infections it cannot answer, such as diarrhoea and pneumonia. There is no effective treatment; it dies or is put down, typically before three months of age.
